newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel continues to trade higher.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel continues to trade higher.

text.p: Singapore gas oil traded higher on Thursday along with firmer swaps values and more optimistic sentiment, but traders said the overall undertone remained bearish.
Two cargoes totalling 350,000 barrels were traded at $20.70 per barrel for August 1-5 lifting free-on-board (fob) basis, 10 cents over Wednesday's solitary deal.
The first 200,000-barrel cargo was sold by a Singapore refiner to a US trader, while the second 150,000-barrel lot was sold by a US major to a Singapore trader.
Sources said the US trader might be looking to ship the cargo westwards, following the three cargoes scheduled for shipment to South America.
Swaps gas oil for August gained 25 cents to be last quoted at $21.60/$21.70 per barrel, while September was flat to 10 cents higher to be indicated at $22.45/$22.55.

Nepal bought 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil from Shell at $162.69 per tonne for August 11-20 lifting and from BB Energy at $163.44 per tonne for August 21-31 delivery, cost-and-freight (c+f) Madras/Haldia.
Nepal was expected to issue another gas oil import tender in a month's time for September delivery.
Jet fuel was also actively offered with four sellers--a US trader, a Chinese trader and two US majors offering august lifting cargoes at between $23.60 and $24.00 per barrel.
Only one bid was seen, from a Singapore trader, at $23.00 fob, was no deals were concluded.
Traders still maintained that jet fuel prices were overvalued.
Jet fuel was traded on Wednesday at $23.50 per barrel for early August lifting, fob.

Traders said Indonesia recently bought an August jet fuel cargo from a US major at a 10-20-per-barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, fob basis. They said this reflected the low value of the product.
